reading.title: The price of looking rich
reading.text: Economists use the term conspicuous consumption for buying expensive goods mainly so that others will notice them. From a historical perspective, this is nothing new: wealthy Romans built spectacular villas for the same reason. What has changed is the audience. Social media turns every friend into a spectator, and many young people suspect that their followers judge them by what they own. In retrospect, some admit that the designer bags and new phones damaged their financial prospects. Researchers who inspected the spending data of 5,000 graduates found that the most image-conscious saved 40 percent less.
